cores.Primary Function: Base Saturation Tone — Ideal for large areas of colour (e.g. shields, robes). High saturation colour, requires complementary green for cold shadows.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply in thin layers (layering) to build up saturation in heraldry and robes. Excellent base for glazing more intense reds.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold shadow and natural contrast — green cools the red, ideal for recesses and shadow areas.
cores.Keywords: Shields, Capes, Layering, Glazing, Base Red

cores.Primary Function: Deep Warm Shadow — Used for very dark red shadows, or as a base colour to simulate wine, dried blood or velvet.
cores.Strategic Use: Ideal for wet blending on heavy fabrics like velvet or for simulating dried blood. Use in dark washes to create depth without resorting to black.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Deep cold shadow — great for bases with dramatic lighting. Avoids "too warm" tones.
cores.Keywords: Shadows, Dried Blood, Velvet, Wet Blending, Wine, Recess Shading

cores.Primary Function: Base/Intermediate Tone — Warm and vibrant colour, excellent for highlights of earth tones or as a base for reddish and rusty wood.
cores.Strategic Use: Use in light drybrush for warm highlights on reddish wood or leather. Apply with stippling to create rust or earth texture.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold complementary contrast. Ideal for metallic reflections and steel shine near warm tones.
cores.Keywords: Rust, Leather, Wood, Drybrush, Stippling, Warm Highlight

cores.Primary Function: Base Tone/Cold Saturation — The classic vivid blue. Used for fabrics (cloaks) and cavalry emblems. Requires complementary Orange for warm highlights.
cores.Strategic Use: Perfect for glazing on cloaks and emblems, building depth and smooth blends. Use in layers to obtain a vibrant and uniform blue.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Highlight Contrast: Being a light and cold blue, a light orange creates the perfect contrast to simulate sun reflection on blue metallic surfaces or warning lights.
cores.Keywords: Blue Cloaks, Cavalry, Smooth Blending, Glazing, Emblems

cores.Primary Function: Base Tone/Blue Highlight — Lighter and less saturated blue than Ultramarine. Ideal for cold base layers or for highlighting edges of darker blues.
cores.Strategic Use: Essential for edge highlighting on bluish armour or fine fabrics. Can be mixed with skin tones to create realistic cold shadows.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Warm light and subtle reflections — maintains balance between cold and warm tones.
cores.Keywords: Edge Highlighting, Blue Armour, Skin Shadows, Cold Light

cores.Primary Function: Cold Shadow Tone/Bluish Metal — Excellent for deep shadows of blue fabrics or as a base tone for aged and dark steel.
cores.Strategic Use: Base for non-metallic metal (NMM) in aged steel tones. Use in dark washes for deep shadows in blues without "dirtying" the colour.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Strong contrast (warm analogue) — excellent for adding tones of dust, dirt or rust, creating an earthy realism.
cores.Keywords: NMM, Aged Steel, Deep Shadow, Deep Wash, Black Armour

cores.Primary Function: Neutral/Warm Base Tone — Used for cloaks and scrolls and as a base colour for mortar or light stone in dioramas.
cores.Strategic Use: Versatile base for scrolls, bones and cloaks. Excellent for receiving earth tone washes and for texturing light stone surfaces.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold shadow for skin tones, leather or fabrics. Helps give depth without darkening too much.
cores.Keywords: Scrolls, Bones, Tabards, Light Stone, Mortar, Base Coating

cores.Primary Function: Highlight/Light Point — The lightest tone for Beige fabric highlights or for the most illuminated points of stone/bone.
cores.Strategic Use: Ideal for final highlights on scrolls, purity seals etc. Use for detailed freehand writing with a fine-tip brush over Beige bases. Perfect colour for illuminating the sharpest edges of bone surfaces or light fabrics.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Soft cold shadows — balance warm light, ideal for light or bone surfaces.
cores.Keywords: Freehand, Purity Seals, Maximum Highlight, Teeth, Bone

cores.Primary Function: Maximum Highlight/Pure White — Used sparingly for metal shines, eyes, crosses on shields and the top of your OSL effect. Never use directly for large areas.
cores.Strategic Use: Use for precise light points on non-metallic surfaces (eyes, crosses). Crucial base for transparent colours and for secondary glow in OSL effects.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Chromatic Cold Shadowing: As Offwhite is an almost white "eggshell" tone, using a diluted violet/blue in the shadows prevents the piece from looking dirty, giving an ethereal and clean appearance.
cores.Keywords: OSL, Eyes, Crosses, Specular Highlight, Light Point

cores.Primary Function: Maximum Light (OSL/LED) — The brightest point for lighting (peak light). Being fluorescent, it amplifies the light of your amber/yellow LED, giving an incandescent and ultra-realistic glow to the lantern bulb.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply over white base to maximise the OSL (Object Source Lighting) effect of lamps and flames. Use in thin layers (layering) to build up luminous intensity.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Intensity Contrast: Essential for the light effect (OSL). Deep purple placed around the yellow source makes the glow appear to emit real light by pure chromatic contrast.
cores.Keywords: LED, Lantern, Glow Effect, OSL, Fluorescent

cores.Primary Function: Base Tone/Warm Highlight — Mainly for skin painting. Also useful as a warm, yellowish highlight for stone and earth textures, complementing your Beige.
cores.Strategic Use: Fundamental colour to illuminate the high volumes of the face (forehead, nose and cheekbones). Can be used to simulate the warm sun reflection hitting the staircase stones through soft drybrushing technique.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Organic Shadowing: For skin, using a diluted dark blue in shadows (like under the chin or eye sockets) neutralises the orange skin tone, creating realistic depth.
cores.Keywords: Faces, Skin, Sunlight, Drybrush, Volumes

cores.Primary Function: Absolute Shadow / Occlusion: Used for separation between materials (e.g. line between belt and tunic) and for mixing with other colours to create deep shadow tones.
cores.Strategic Use: Essential for blacklining, defining contours and separating materials. Base for dark NMM and for occlusion shadows where light does not reach.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Binary Contrast: Technically black has no complementary on the colour wheel, but its role is absolute contrast. White serves to define shapes through edge highlighting.
cores.Keywords: Blacklining, Black Armour, Occlusion, Absolute Shadow, Contours

cores.Primary Function: Neutral Transition Tone: Ideal for painting stone surfaces, metal weathering or for softening the transition between black and white without saturation.
cores.Strategic Use: Use in drybrush to simulate stone or concrete texture. Mix to soften transitions between black and white, avoiding too harsh contrasts.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Weathering Contrast: On grey stones, shadows or stains of an earthy red simulate oxidation, accumulated dirt or exposed bricks under plaster.
cores.Keywords: Stone, Concrete, Neutral Transition, Drybrush, London

cores.Primary Function: Specular Highlight / Mixture: Unlike Offwhite, this is "Pure White". Used only at the exact point where light reflects (glow point) or to lighten highly saturated colours. Essential as a "spot primer" for transparent colours (Fluors/Gels). Without it, the fluorescent pigment has nowhere to "bounce" the light.
cores.Strategic Use: Reserved for the extreme specular highlight point. Use as a spot primer for fluorescent or transparent colours, enhancing their vividness.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Volume Definition: Black serves to create technical delineation (Black Lining) around white, preventing the colour from "blowing out" and losing visual shape.
cores.Keywords: Pure White, Spot Primer, Specular Highlight, Mixtures, Shine

cores.Primary Function: Organic Depth Filter: Excellent for shadows on red fabrics or for giving "life" to skin areas (dark circles, lips or scars) as it is a rich and deep colour.
cores.Strategic Use: Excellent for creating rich and organic shadows on red fabrics. Use very diluted as a glaze to apply in skin recesses, giving a more realistic and "alive" look to faces and scars.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Vibrancy Contrast: Mint green is the direct opposite. Using small points of green in the maximum highlights of a violet cloak makes the colour "pop" to the observer's eye.
cores.Keywords: Scars, Dark Circles, Alive Skin, Red Shadow, Organic Glazing

cores.Primary Function: Cold Light Contrast: Perfect for simulating moonlight reflections or cold light on metallic/leather surfaces. Acts as the "negative" of orange to balance light.
cores.Strategic Use: Use as a filter on metals to simulate moonlight reflections. Apply in fine highlights on leather to balance warm tones and give a touch of freshness.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold Light Contrast / Reflection
cores.Keywords: Moonlight, Cold Reflection, Cold Metal, Thermal Contrast

cores.Primary Function: Energy Effect / OSL (Object Source Lighting): The light point for magic effects or bluish steel reflections under intense light. Due to fluorescence, it "vibrates" more than normal blue.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply over white base for magic energy or plasma effects. Thin layers (layering) build an intense glow, ideal for OSL on blue light sources.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Vibrant OSL Contrast
cores.Keywords: Energy, Plasma, Magic, Blue OSL, Vibrant

cores.Primary Function: Sunlight Highlight: The ideal colour for making the "light point" on warm colours (red, skin, yellow). Gives a natural light appearance instead of artificial light.
cores.Strategic Use: Use in fine highlights to simulate direct intense sunlight on warm colours (reds, oranges). Mix for light skin tones.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Complementary Shadow: Instead of using black to shade yellow (which would create an ugly sludge green), use purple to create deep, rich and natural shadows.
cores.Keywords: Sunlight, Warm Highlight, Final Highlight, Light Skin

cores.Primary Function: Realistic Dirt Filter: Its function is to unify textures (such as leather or earth) and create automatic shadows in 0.04mm grooves. It is the "doctor" of painting.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply in washes on leather or earth to unify textures and create automatic shadows in recesses. Works as a filter for ageing and dirt.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Thermal Neutralisation: Umber is a very warm brown. If the dirt looks "too warm", a little blue neutralises the tone, turning it into a more realistic greyish brown.
cores.Keywords: Wash, Dirt, Unify, Leather, Earth, Recess Shading

cores.Primary Function: Cold Natural Base Tone — Ideal for vegetation, peasant-inspired cloaks and organic elements. Excellent for contrast with earthy tones and warm reds.
cores.Strategic Use: Use as a base for moss and small vegetation growing in brick cracks or between stone steps. Recommended to apply with the brush tip in quick, irregular taps (stippling) to create a natural plant texture.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold shadow and natural contrast — green cools the red, ideal for recesses and shadow areas.
cores.Keywords: Moss, Vegetation, Stippling, Natural

cores.Primary Function: Deep Cold Shadow — Perfect for vegetation shadows, heavy fabrics and areas needing depth without resorting to black.
cores.Strategic Use: The perfect colour for the deepest recession shading in red cloaks and capes. Being the complementary colour of red, it creates a much more realistic and technically "correct" shadow than using just black paint.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Deep cold shadow — great for bases with dramatic lighting. Avoids "too warm" tones.
cores.Keywords: Red Shadow, Capes, Cold Shadow, Forest, Depth

cores.Primary Function: Contrast Cold — Ideal for creating aged metallic reflections, light oxidation and complementary contrast in warm schemes.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply as a filter on metals to simulate verdigris (copper oxidation) or reflections on ancient armour. Adds a unique chromatic interest.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold complementary contrast. Ideal for metallic reflections and steel shine near warm tones.
cores.Keywords: Verdigris, Oxidation, Copper, Cold Filter

cores.Primary Function: Warm Sunlight Highlight — Excellent for illuminating fabrics, leather and gold metals while maintaining chromatic richness without resorting to pure yellow.
cores.Strategic Use: Use in glazing on reds to intensify heat. Apply in fine highlights on gold or bronze to simulate reflection of flames or embers.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Warm contrast — perfect for light and highlight in illuminated areas.
cores.Keywords: Embers, Flames, Gold Highlight, Heat, Warm Glazing

cores.Primary Function: Warm Earthy Shadow — Ideal for aged leather, rich rust and organic shadows on red fabrics.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply with stippling to simulate old rust, hard earth or very worn leather. Use in washes to create a "dirty" and heavy realism.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Strong contrast (warm analogue) — excellent for adding tones of dust, dirt or rust, creating an earthy realism.
cores.Keywords: Hard Earth, Old Rust, Old Leather, Stippling, Dirt

cores.Primary Function: Chromatic Cold Shadow — Perfect for enriching shadows of skin, leather or light fabrics without "dirtying" with black.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply in glazing on shadows of skin, leather or light fabrics to enrich colour without "dirtying". Works as a filter for whites and greys.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold shadow for skin tones, leather or fabrics. Helps give depth without darkening too much.
cores.Keywords: Clean Shadow, Skin Glazing, Filter for White, Chromatic

cores.Primary Function: Deep Luxury Shadow — Excellent for noble fabrics, dramatic areas and depth in high contrast compositions.
cores.Strategic Use: Ideal for wet blending on luxurious fabrics or for creating dramatic contrasts in fantasy figures. Excellent base for painting gems and crystals.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Soft cold shadows — balance warm light, ideal for light or bone surfaces.
cores.Keywords: Gems, Crystals, Nobility, Wet Blending, Dramatic Shadow

cores.Primary Function: High Reflectivity Noble Metal — Pure high-shine silver for knightly armour, templar sword blades and silverware details.
cores.Strategic Use: Being from the Metal Color line, fluidity is incredible. Ideal for airbrush or brush in thin layers. Use for final highlights (edge highlighting) over darker metals to simulate the blade edge.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Reflection Shadow: Deep blue simulates sky reflection or cold shadows on polished metal, essential for depth in TMM.
cores.Keywords: Silver, Armour, Sword, Metal Color, TMM, High Shine

cores.Primary Function: Imperial / Heraldic Gold — Rich gold tone for sword hilt details, ornamental crosses and buckles. Offers superior metallic coverage without lumps.
cores.Strategic Use: Excellent for fine detail painting with a brush. For shadows, mix slightly with an Umber Wash for an aged gold or keep pure for new and polished gold.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Royalty Contrast: Deep purple in gold shadows creates a classic chromatic contrast that makes the golden shine appear much more intense.
cores.Keywords: Gold, Golden, Ornaments, Heraldry, Luxury, TMM

cores.Primary Function: The 'Liquid Talent' — Low surface tension black shade designed to flow directly into recesses for instant definition.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply generously over metals or cold colours to create technical depth. Essential for engine parts and armour where panel separation is critical.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Maximum definition contrast.
cores.Keywords: Liquid Talent, Shade, Definition, Recess Shading, Wash

cores.Primary Function: Universal Organic Shadow — Earthy brown shade for shading golds, leathers, woods, and skin tones.
cores.Strategic Use: Ideal for giving a 'used' and realistic look to organic materials. In your diorama, use to shade cracks between stones and bricks for accumulated dirt.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Neutralisation of excessive warm tones.
cores.Keywords: Dirt, Organic, Shade, Leather, Ageing

cores.Primary Function: Industrial Streaking Dirt — The definitive product for the 'Grimdark' style. Simulates years of pollution and rain accumulation on vertical surfaces.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply over the whole piece, let dry for 15 mins and remove excess with a cotton bud and Thinner. It leaves only the recesses dirty and creates ultra-realistic transition filters.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Clean vs dirty surface contrast.
cores.Keywords: Grimdark, Enamel, Weathering, Industrial, Realism

cores.Primary Function: Base Metallic Paint (Steel) — The foundational colour for most silver-toned metals, such as weapons, armour, and mechanical components. Excellent coverage over black primers.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply as a solid basecoat for all metallic elements. Serves as the perfect foundation for shading with Nuln Oil and highlighting with Stormhost Silver.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Shade to define recesses and add depth; Highlight to simulate worn edges and light reflection points.
cores.Keywords: Metallic, Steel, Weapons, Armour, TMM, Metallic Base

cores.Primary Function: Base Metallic Paint (Gold) — A rich, opaque gold colour, ideal for golden armours, ornaments, and elite details. Known for its superior coverage.
cores.Strategic Use: Use as a basecoat for all gold elements. Shade with Reikland Fleshshade for a warm, deep tone. Highlight with Liberator Gold or Stormhost Silver.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Shade to enrich the gold tone, adding depth and an appearance of ancient gold.
cores.Keywords: Metallic, Gold, Armour, TMM, Custodes, Stormcast

cores.Primary Function: Opaque Base Black — Foundational black colour for primers, basecoats, armour panels, and for correcting mistakes. Smooth and consistent finish.
cores.Strategic Use: Ideal for Black Legion armour or the under-suits of Space Marines. Use as a base for highlighting with greys like Eshin Grey and Dawnstone to create volume.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Highlight to define edges and surfaces, creating contrast and avoiding a 'flat' appearance.
cores.Keywords: Black, Base, Armour, Black Legion, Corrector

cores.Primary Function: Vibrant Base Red — A deep, highly opaque red, perfect for armour (Blood Angels), robes, and lenses. Excellent coverage.
cores.Strategic Use: Apply as a basecoat for any red area. Shade with Agrax Earthshade for a dirty tone or Carroburg Crimson for a richer red. Highlight with Evil Sunz Scarlet.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Cold shadow to create a more dramatic and natural contrast in the deepest recesses.
cores.Keywords: Red, Blood Angels, Robes, Lenses, Base

cores.Primary Function: Iconic Base Blue — The standard blue for Ultramarines. A dark, rich primary blue, very versatile for power armour and uniforms.
cores.Strategic Use: Basecoat for Ultramarines' armour and other factions. Shade with Nuln Oil for a clean finish or Drakenhof Nightshade for more depth. Highlight with Calgar Blue.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Contrast for details like lenses or small symbols, creating a strong point of visual interest.
cores.Keywords: Blue, Ultramarines, Power Armour, Base

cores.Primary Function: Flesh/Bone Base Tone — A versatile, warm off-white. Ideal for bone, parchment, pale skin, cloth, and light-coloured stone.
cores.Strategic Use: Use as a basecoat for any bone or parchment elements. Shade with Agrax Earthshade or Seraphim Sepia for an aged look. Highlight with Pallid Wych Flesh.
cores.Role of Complementary (Shadow, Reflectio: Shade to create a warm, aged tone, perfect for organic materials like bone and papyrus.
cores.Keywords: Bone, Parchment, Pale Skin, Stone, Base

efeitos.Function: Rust/Weathering Effect (Enamel): Rust-coloured liquid used to simulate streaks of rusted metal on vehicles, armour or stone surfaces near metal objects. Applied in fine lines and then softened with Enamel Thinner.
Concrete/Cement Texture: Thick acrylic-based product, ready for use, simulating concrete texture and colour. Ideal for creating foundations, floors or walls at the base of your diorama.

Dark Steel Pigment (Powder): Ultrafine powder used to create dust, dirt effects, or to polish metal surfaces (like the knight's chainmail), giving a realistic dark metallic shine. Applied dry or fixed with pigment fixer.
efeitos.Keywords: Pigment, Steel, Polishing, Chainmail, Realistic Metal

efeitos.Function: Green Moss Texture: Acrylic product simulating moss and lichen on surfaces. Great for adding life and moisture to stones, providing contrast with grey or reddish rock.
Satin Varnish (Acrylic): Varnish with an intermediate finish between matt and gloss. Ideal for giving a slight "moisture" shine or for protecting colours that should not be fully matt.
efeitos.Keywords: Varnish, Satin, Protection, Light Shine, Acrylic

efeitos.Function: White Sealer/Primer (Acrylic): White base to prepare the surface (plastic, resin, metal, stone). Essential to ensure paint adhesion and make bright colours more vibrant.
efeitos.Keywords: Primer, White, Adhesion, Vibrant Colours, Preparatory Base

efeitos.Function: Black Sealer/Primer (Acrylic): Black base. Great for pre-shading and for dark colours. Helps define recesses and gives immediate depth to the miniature.
Acrylic Thinner: Used to dilute AK acrylic paints and primers, whether for airbrush application or to create smoother and more controlled washes with a brush.
Gravel and Sand Fixer (Liquid): Transparent glue/liquid used to fix sand, gravel, small stones and grass flocks to the diorama base, ensuring they do not come loose.
efeitos.Keywords: Fixer, Sand, Gravel, Diorama Glue, Base Building

efeitos.Function: NATO Camouflage Colour: Standard brown used on modern NATO military vehicles. Ideal for military dioramas or for simulating dried mud and hard earth on bases.
efeitos.Keywords: Dried Mud, Military, NATO, Camouflage, Earth

efeitos.Function: Extreme Snow Effect: White microsphere powder that simulates the texture of fresh fallen snow. Can be mixed with resin or gloss varnish for melting snow.
Fresh Blood Effect: Technical paint with a glossy, viscous finish that remains looking 'wet' even after drying.
Shade for Flesh and Warm Tones: A reddish-brown wash that adds depth and warmth to skin tones, gold, bronze, and reds.
efeitos.Keywords: Shade, Wash, Skin, Gold, Bronze, Effect
